dcterms:title: The Dystopian Line
dcterms:description: A chain of government-surveillance novels, each written partly in conversation with the last. The earliest, We, was suppressed by a government; the latest, a graphic adaptation, by school districts.

dcterms:title: Coming of Age and the Perks Reading List
dcterms:description: Young-adult novels that place classic books inside their stories. The Perks of Being a Wallflower is a hub: its narrator's reading list links one of the most challenged books of 2025 to five challenged classics.

dcterms:title: African American Literary Lineage
dcterms:description: Works that answer, extend, or revise one another across a century, several of them among the most consistently challenged books in ALA's records.

dcterms:title: Testimony and Graphic Narrative
dcterms:description: Memoir and testimony, much of it in comics form. The format itself is often the stated reason for challenge, which is why the graphic adaptation of Anne Frank's diary is targeted separately from the diary.

dcterms:title: Myth, Epic, and Retelling
dcterms:description: Works that retell or rework older stories. Some sources (the Odyssey, Beowulf, fairy tales) are rarely challenged themselves; the retellings are.

dcterms:title: Obscenity-Era Classics and Title Allusions
dcterms:description: Twentieth-century classics challenged for language, sexuality, or politics. Many take their titles from older texts, which places those older texts in the network as well.
